1.note: The author is using the word **And** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event. Alternate translation: [Now these]

The phrase **on the day** is a common expression of this culture to mean “when.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [when]

3.note: It might seem that the expression **These are the names of the sons of Aaron** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language, since the same words are in the previous verse. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [They are the priests]

The expressions **the ones who were anointed** and **whose hand he filled** are describing the same priests, not distinguishing between different priests. They are not making a distinction between the priests and the ones who were anointed or whose hand he filled. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this relationship between these phrases clearer. Alternate translation: [that is, the ones who were anointed and whose hand he filled]

The expression **who were anointed** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is Moses. Alternate translation: [the ones whom Moses anointed]

In this verse, the words **hand** and **priest** are singular in form, but they refer to all the priests as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural forms of “hand” and “priest.” Alternate translation: [whose hands he filled to serve as priests]

The author is using **whose hand he filled** as a common expression of his culture to mean “whom he dedicated as priests.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [whom he dedicated]

4.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the words “and Abihu” before the word “died.” Alternate translation: [But Nadab and Abihu died]

Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in the presence of … in the presence of]

Here, **strange fire** represents burning coals that were not authorized for use in worship, as indicated in the account of this event in Leviticus 10:1. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [strange coals that were on fire]

Here, the author is speaking of fire that was not authorized as if it were **strange** or foreign. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [unauthorized fire]

The author is using **sons were not to them** as a common expression of his culture to mean “they had no sons.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and they had no sons]

The word **And** here indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [As a result, only Eleazar served as priest and Ithamar]

If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about Eleazar and Ithamar together by saying that they both served as priests. Alternate translation: [And Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests]

The author is using **against the face of** as a common expression of his culture to mean “under the supervision of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [under the supervision of Aaron]

5.note: The author is using the word translated **And** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event. Alternate translation: [Now Yahweh spoke]
Here and throughout the chapter, the word **saying** introduces a direct quotation. See how you translated **saying** in [1:1](ta:01).

6.note: Yahweh is using this possessive form to mean the **tribe** that has the name **Levi**. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. See how you translated this phrase in 1:21. Alternate translation: [Levi tribe] or [the tribe that is named Levi]
Here, **it** refers to all the men of **the tribe of Levi**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state this explicitly. Alternate translation: [the men from the tribe]
See how you translated the same use of this phrase in 3:4.

7.note: For emphasis, people in this culture used a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. Here and throughout this chapter, this happens with the words **keep** and **keeping**. See the chapter introduction for more information. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of showing the emphasis. Alternate translation: [And they shall carefully keep him and all the congregation]

Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of the tent of meeting. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in front of the tent of meeting]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **service**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to serve what needs to be served for the Dwelling]

Here, the phrase **to serve** could introduce: (1) something that happens at the same time as the “keeping” earlier in the verse. Alternate translation: [while serving] (2) the means by which they do the “keeping” earlier in the verse. Alternate translation: [by serving]

8.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **vessels** that are characterized by being used in **the tent of meeting**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the vessels that are used in the tent of meeting]
See how you translated this phrase in 3:7.

9.q: וְ⁠נָתַתָּה֙ אֶת־הַ⁠לְוִיִּ֔ם לְ⁠אַהֲרֹ֖ן וּ⁠לְ⁠בָנָ֑י⁠ו נְתוּנִ֨ם נְתוּנִ֥ם הֵ֨מָּה֙ ל֔⁠וֹ
9.note: Here, Yahweh is speaking as if the Levites were actually objects that could be given to Aaron and his sons. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And you shall assign the Levites to Aaron and to his sons. They are assigned, assigned to him]
The word **you** is singular here because Yahweh is speaking to Moses. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

The expression **are given, given** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is God. Alternate translation: [I have given them, given them]

Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **given** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [They are wholly given]

The implication is that **him** refers to **Aaron and his sons**, who were just mentioned. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [to Aaron and his sons]

10.note: The implication is that **count** means to appoint or assign Aaron and his sons as priests. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And you shall appoint as priests]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **priesthood**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what they do as priests]
See how you translated this sentence in 1:51.

12.note: Yahweh is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb translated as **I have taken** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that he is the one who has chosen the Levites. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing that emphasis. Alternate translation: [And behold, I am the one who has taken]

Yahweh is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [listen]

Here, Yahweh is speaking as if choosing the Levites were actually **taking** them **from the midst of the sons of Israel**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I … have selected the Levites from]

The implication is that Yahweh has **taken the Levites** to serve him at the tent of meeting. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [I … have taken the Levites to minister to me in the tent of meeting]

It might seem that the expression **firstborn, the opener of the womb** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [firstborn]

Here and throughout the chapter, the implication is that **firstborn** refers specifically to firstborn males. See the chapter introduction for more information. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [firstborn male]

Yahweh is using **the opener of the womb** as a common expression of the culture to mean “first child to be born to a woman.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the first child of every woman]

The word **and** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [and as a result, the Levites shall be for me]

13.note: See how you translated this phrase in [3:1](ta:03).

By **striking down**, Yahweh means that he killed the firstborn Egyptians. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. See the discussion of the term “struck” in the Introduction to Numbers. Alternate translation: [my slaying]
Here, **Israel** refers to the people who descended from **Israel**. See the discussion of this in the book introduction.

The expression **from man up to animal** is a common expression of this culture to mean “both humans and animals.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [both men and animals]

Here the masculine term **man** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [from human]

15.note: Here, Yahweh is speaking of **the sons of Levi** as if they were Levi’s direct children, but he is actually referring to all men who were descended from Levi. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the men descended from Levi]

Here and throughout this chapter, the phrase **house of their fathers** refers to largest divisions within a single tribe. The word **clans** refers to the largest divisions of each **house of their fathers**. See the chapter introduction for more information. Alternate translation: [according to the house of their fathers, according to the clans that make up each house of their fathers]
See how you translated this phrase in 1:2.

It might seem that the expression **You shall count them** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language since it repeats the command from the first part of the verse. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [according to their clans, every male]

Here and throughout this chapter, the phrase **from a son of a month and upward** is a common expression of this culture to mean “someone who is at least one month old.” See the chapter introduction for more information. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [every male who is one month old or older]

16.note: The word **And** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [As a result, Moses counted them]

It might seem that the expression **upon the mouth of Yahweh, just as he was commanded** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [exactly as he was commanded by Yahweh]

The author is using **upon the mouth of Yahweh** as a common expression of his culture to mean “according to what Yahweh said.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [as Yahweh had said]

The expression **he was commanded** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is God. Alternate translation: [Yahweh commanded him]

19.note: The implication is that these are names of Kohath’s sons. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And these are the names of the sons of Kohath according to their clans:]

20.note: The implication is that these are names of Merari’s sons. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And these are the names of the sons of Merari according to their clans:]

It might seem that the expression **These are they, the clans of** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [These are the clans of the Levites]

21.note: The author is using this possessive form to mean descendants and clans that came from Gershon. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Descended from Gershon]
**Libnite** refers to a descendant of Libni, **Shimeite** refers to a descendant of Shimei, and **Gershonite** refers to a descendant of Gershon.

Here, **the Libnite**, **the Shimeite**, and **the Gershonite** represent groups of people in general, not specific individuals. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use expressions that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the Libnites … the Shimeites … the Gershonites]
See how you translated this clause in 3:20.

22.q: פְּקֻדֵי⁠הֶם֙ בְּ⁠מִסְפַּ֣ר כָּל־זָכָ֔ר מִ⁠בֶּן־חֹ֖דֶשׁ וָ⁠מָ֑עְלָ⁠ה פְּקֻ֣דֵי⁠הֶ֔ם שִׁבְעַ֥ת אֲלָפִ֖ים וַ⁠חֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵאֽוֹת
22.note: It might seem that the expression **their counted ones** being repeated contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [Their counted ones by the number of every male from a son of a month and upward were 7,500]

The expression **their counted ones** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is Moses. Alternate translation: [Those whom Moses counted … those whom Moses counted]
If your language has a different way of expressing the number **7,500**, you could use that number expression instead. Alternate translation: [were seventy-five hundred]

23.note: See how you translated this phrase in 3:21.

24.note: See how you translated this phrase is in 3:23.

25.note: Here, **sons** refers to male descendants. See how you translated the same use of **sons** in 3:15.

Here, the word **Dwelling** refers specifically to the inner part of the sacred tent, made out of ten curtains. The word **tent** refers specifically to the outer part of the sacred tent, made out of eleven curtains. See Exodus 26:1–13 for details. You could indicate these details explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the inner curtains and the outer curtains of the Dwelling]

The implication is that this was the covering that went over the entire tent. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the covering over the tent]

26.note: The implication is that these were the curtains that marked off and formed a fence around the courtyard, as described in Exodus 27:9–15. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and the curtains that marked off the courtyard]

The author is using **on the Dwelling and on the altar all around** as a common expression of his culture to mean “that contains the sacred tent and the altar.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [that contains the Dwelling and the altar]

Here, the pronoun **its** could refer to: (1) the curtains mentioned in this and the previous verse. Alternate translation: [and the ropes for the curtains for all their service] (2) the Dwelling. Alternate translation: [and the ropes for the Dwelling for all its service]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **service**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [for all the ways that it needs to be served]

27.note: See how you translated the similar phrase in 3:21.

**Amramite** refers to a descendant of Amram, **Izharite** refers to a descendant of Izhar, **Hebronite** refers to a descendant of **Hebron**, **Uzzielite** refers to a descendant of Uzziel, and **Kohathite** refers to a descendant of Kohath.

The author is not referring to a specific **Amramite**, **Izharite**, **Hebronite**, **Uzzielite**, or **Kohathite**. He means all the people in each of these clans. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the Amramites … the Izharites … the Hebronites … the Uzzielites … the Kohathites]
See how you translated this clause in 3:20.

28.note: If your language has a different way of expressing the number **8,600**, you could use that number expression instead. Alternate translation: [eighty-six hundred]

29.note: Here, **sons** refers to male descendants. See how you translated the same use of **sons** in 3:15.

30.note: See how you translated this phrase is in 3:27.

31.note: The implication is that this was the special table that held the bread that was presented to God. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and the table for the special bread]
The pronoun **they** could refer to: (1) the priests. Alternate translation: [the priests minister] (2) the Kohathites. Alternate translation: [the descendants of Kohath minister]

The implication is that this was the special curtain that separated the Most Holy Place from the Holy Place in the sacred tent. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and the curtain that separated the Most Holy Place from the Holy Place]

Here, the pronoun **its** could refer to: (1) just the curtain. Alternate translation: [and all the service for the curtain] (2) all the items mentioned in this verse. Alternate translation: [and all the service for all those things]
See how you translated this phrase in 3:26. Alternate translation: [and all the ways that it needs to be served]

32.note: The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and he had the oversight of]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **oversight**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [overseeing]

33.note: See how you translated the similar phrase in 3:21.
**Mahlite** refers to a descendant of Mahli, and **Mushite** refers to a descendant of Mushi.

The author is not referring to a specific **Mahlite** and **Mushite**. He means all the people from these clans. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the Mahlites … the Mushites]
See how you translated this clause in 3:20.

34.note: If your language has a different way of expressing the number **6,200**, you could use that number expression instead. Alternate translation: [were sixty-two hundred]

36.note: See how you translated the abstract noun **oversight** in 3:32. Alternate translation: [And the sons of Merari oversaw the keeping of]
Here, **sons** refers to male descendants. See how you translated the same use of **sons** in 3:15.

Here, **frames** refers to open wooden structures made to hold the curtains. If a translation is available in your language, see how it translates this term in Exodus 26:15. Alternate translation: [the wooden structural supports of the Dwelling]

Here, **crossbars** refers to horizontal support beams that give stability to the structure. If a translation is available in your language, see how it translates this term in Exodus 26:26. Alternate translation: [and the beams that support it]

These **bases** were silver blocks that had a slot in them to keep the pillars in place and off the ground. If a translation is available in your language, see how it translates this term in Exodus 26:19. Alternate translation: [and its metal foundations]
See how you translated this phrase in 3:26. Alternate translation: [and all the ways that it needs to be served]

37.note: The implication is that these pillars formed a fence that marked off the boundary of the courtyard around the sacred tent. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and the posts that mark off the courtyard]

Here, **bases**, **pegs**, and **ropes** refer to the items used to secure the pillars and curtains of the courtyard fence into place. The pillars were placed on the **bases**, **ropes** were fastened to them, and the other ends of the **ropes** were fastened down with the **pegs**, which were driven into the ground. Alternate translation: [and their metal foundations and their spikes and their cords]

38.q: לִ⁠פְנֵ֣י הַ⁠מִּשְׁכָּ֡ן קֵ֣דְמָ⁠ה לִ⁠פְנֵי֩ אֹֽהֶל־מוֹעֵ֨ד ׀ מִזְרָ֜חָ⁠ה
38.note: These two phrases **to the face of the Dwelling to the east** and **to the face of the tent of meeting toward the sunrise** mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [to the face of the tent of meeting to the east]

Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of the Dwelling and the tent of meeting. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before the Dwelling … before the tent of meeting]
See how you translated this sentence in 1:51.

39.q: כָּל־פְּקוּדֵ֨י הַ⁠לְוִיִּ֜ם אֲשֶׁר֩ פָּקַ֨ד מֹשֶׁ֧ה וְׄ⁠אַׄהֲׄרֹ֛ׄןׄ
39.note: It might seem that the expression **All the counted ones of the Levites whom Moses and Aaron counted** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [All the Levites whom Moses and Aaron counted]
See how you translated this passive form in 3:22.
See how you translated this phrase in 3:16.
If your language has a different way of expressing the number **22,000**, you could use that number expression instead. Alternate translation: [were twenty-two thousand]

40.note: This sentence could refer to: (1) calculating the total **number** of **names**. Alternate translation: [And calculate the number of their names] (2) writing down a list of **names**. Alternate translation: [And list their names]
The pronoun **their** refers to the firstborn males of Israel. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the names of those counted]

41.q: וְ⁠לָקַחְתָּ֨ אֶת־הַ⁠לְוִיִּ֥ם לִ⁠י֙ אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה תַּ֥חַת
41.note: Yahweh interrupts the sentence with the statement **I am Yahweh** in order to remind Moses of who he is. If it would be more natural in your language, you could change the order of these clauses. Alternate translation: [Remember that I am Yahweh. You shall take the Levites for me instead of]

In this verse, the word **animal** is singular in form, but it refers to all livestock as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “animal.” Alternate translation: [the animals of the Levites … among the animals of the sons of Israel]

42.q: וַ⁠יִּפְקֹ֣ד מֹשֶׁ֔ה כַּ⁠אֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֹת֑⁠וֹ אֶֽת־כָּל־בְּכֹ֖ר בִּ⁠בְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
42.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about Yahweh commanding Moses before the information about Moses counting the people. Alternate translation: [And just as Yahweh had commanded him, Moses counted all the firstborn among the sons of Israel]
**And** here introduces the result of obeying the instructions stated in the previous clause. See how you translated the same use of **And** in 3:16.

43.note: See how you translated this phrase in 1:2.
See how you translated **their counted ones** in 3:22.

43.q: שְׁנַ֤יִם וְ⁠עֶשְׂרִים֙ אֶ֔לֶף שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה וְ⁠שִׁבְעִ֖ים וּ⁠מָאתָֽיִם
43.note: If your language has a different way of expressing the number **22,273**, you could use that number expression instead. Alternate translation: [was twenty-two thousand two hundred and seventy-three men]

45.note: The implication is that this refers to firstborn male animals, as stated in 3:41. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [their firstborn male animal]

46.note: Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [And you shall take the ransoms of]

Here, **ransoms** refers to money that must be paid for the additional 273 firstborn mentioned in this verse. Since there were not enough Levites to be in place of these 273 firstborn, God required money in their place. See the discussion of this in the General Notes for this chapter. Alternate translation: [And the payment for the 273]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **ransoms**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And you shall ransom the 273]
If your language has a different way of expressing the number **273**, you could use that number expression instead. Alternate translation: [the two hundred seventy-three]

46.q: הַ⁠שְּׁלֹשָׁ֔ה וְ⁠הַ⁠שִּׁבְעִ֖ים וְ⁠הַ⁠מָּאתָ֑יִם הָ⁠עֹֽדְפִים֙ עַל־הַ⁠לְוִיִּ֔ם מִ⁠בְּכ֖וֹר בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
46.note: The implication is that these were 273 firstborn Israelite males who did not have a corresponding Levite male to take their place. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the 273 firstborn males who did not have a Levite in their place]

This clause gives further information about **the 273**. It is not making a distinction between **the 273** and **the ones being in excess**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make the relationship between these phrases clearer. Alternate translation: [that is, the ones being in excess over the Levites from the firstborn of the sons of Israel]

47.note: In ancient times, a **shekel** was a measure of weight for silver that equaled about 11 grams. You could try to express this in terms of modern money values, but if you did, that could cause your Bible translation to become outdated and inaccurate, since those values can change over time. Instead, you might say something general like “pieces of silver,” or use the biblical term in the text and explain the value in a note.

Yahweh repeats the same word **five** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [precisely five]

Yahweh is using **skull** to represent a whole person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [for each person]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a shekel that was used in **the holy place**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [that is used in the holy place]
